subject: Polaris Retail — live flow slowdowns impacting chat stream
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Alexandra Cruz <axcruz@polarisretail.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 07 Sep 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Observed live-flow slowdowns — initial notice

Hi Alexandra —

We observed elevated tail latency on your live chat streaming endpoints in the us-west region starting ~09:08 PDT. The impact shows as slower token deltas and occasional stalled chunks for sessions originating from your storefront realtime edge.

Quick summary:
- When: 09:08–09:45 PDT (elevated error/slow traces continued intermittently after)
- Impact: increased token latency (median +120ms, p95 up to ~2s) and ~0.7% session stalls for active conversations
- Scope: Polaris production workspaces routed through us-west cluster pool

Immediate actions were taking:
1) Redirecting new streaming requests to a warmed fallback shard (lower model variant) for affected capacity to reduce queuing.
2) Increasing autoscale headroom on your dedicated shard for 30 minutes to clear backed-up KV caches.
3) Capturing session traces — attaching a small sample for your ops team to inspect.

Could you confirm whether you saw any client-side errors or user reports? Well keep this channel updated and follow up with a remediation checklist minutes after the mitigation.

Apologies for the disruption — were prioritizing Polaris while we trace root cause.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Account Lead, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Observed live-flow slowdowns — initial notice / temporary mitigations

Alexandra / Platform Ops —

Thanks for confirming. We pushed a set of short-term mitigations that should reduce user impact while we chase root cause:

Actions completed (live):
- Failover: New streaming requests now route to fallback shard running a smaller model variant (v1-compact) with warmed KV cache. Expect lower quality on very long-context generative flows but much improved token delivery times.
- Autoscale bump: Added +2 GPU headroom to your reserved pool for 30 minutes; queue drained by ~09:58.
- Prefix cache flush: We detected a stale prefix cache invalidation that increased cache misses for a subset of sessions; we performed a controlled flush and warmup.

Client-side mitigations to consider (recommended for the next 1–2 hours):
1) Reduce streaming max_tokens/window_size to lower token-propensity per request.
2) If you surface partial chunks to users, implement a quick client-side retry on a stalled chunk after 800ms.
3) De-prioritize long background scoring jobs from the same session pool during peak.

We attached a short runbook and a sample of session traces we collected. Ben is running a deeper JVM+kernel IO correlation across the shard fleet and will update within 90 minutes.

We will follow up with a brief post-incident write-up by tomorrow that includes timeline, root cause hypothesis, and recommended config changes to avoid recurrence.

Jonas
Account Lead, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Alexandra Cruz <axcruz@polarisretail.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 08 Sep 2028 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Post-incident summary: 2028-09-07 US-WEST live-flow slowdowns (Polaris Retail)

Alexandra —

Short post-incident summary and next steps. Thank you for the responsiveness and for sending additional client traces — that helped shorten the investigation.

Incident snapshot:
- Window of elevated token latency and stalls: 2028-09-07T09:08–2028-09-07T10:30 PDT (primary), with intermittent small regressions through 2028-09-07T12:10 PDT
- Users impacted: ~0.7% of active sessions routed to us-west; focused on long-context checkout assistant flows
- Customer-reported impact: session stalls and increased time-to-first-chunk on web clients during promotional peak

Root cause (summary):
Our investigation shows a confluence of two factors:
1) A regression in our background cache shard selector that introduced elevated cache fragmentation for specific key prefixes used by Polariss session routing. This increased cache miss rates and caused higher KV retrieval latency for hot sessions.
2) A coincident microburst of checkpointing IO on a subset of GPUs servicing the us-west pool (vendor kernel scheduling interaction) that amplified token generation tail latency.

Remediation and durable fixes:
- Immediate code rollback: we reverted the shard-selector change and added a hard guard to prevent prefix fragmentation regressions.
- IO resiliency: scheduler-level backoff and isolations for checkpoint IO; working with hardware partner for firmware tuning (patch tracked in INC-2028-091).
- SLO/observability: added a new streaming KV cache miss alarm (p95) and a dashboard for prefix collision hotspots.

Customer-facing mitigations we recommend (applied or available):
- Use the compact model variant during high promotional peaks to reduce tail latency risk (we can automate this as a routing policy).
- Apply client-side retry for stalled chunk >800ms and lower per-request token window when possible.

Credits & follow-up:
We will apply a one-time service credit for the impacted window and are open to a joint runbook session to automate routing policies for your high-traffic campaigns. Ive created a short PDF summary attached and logged a HubSpot note under deal RDW-4852.

Open next steps (owners):
- Ben Carter: finish hardware scheduler correlation by 2028-09-10 and share findings with Polaris.
- Stephanie Nguyen / Jonas Weber: schedule a 1-hour runbook workshop (automation of fallback routing + client retry) if Polaris is available next week.
- Redwood Eng Ops: follow up on vendor firmware ticket and share ETA.

Attachments: redwood_incident_summary_20280908.pdf, polaris_session_traces_20280907.json

Thanks again for the patience — we appreciate the partnership and will take action to reduce recurrence risk.

Jonas Weber
Account Lead, Customer Reliability
